text:
alex: Customer reports 503s and says there's no trace id in their headers. any quick asks before we escalate?
maria: first ask for the exact request timestamp (UTC) and the full request headers they saw. if they only have an example, that's fine.
ryan: also ask whether they hit hosted or dedicated, and which region. routing matters. :world_map:
emma: minimal checklist I send customers: 1) full HTTP response headers 2) the raw request body (remove secrets) 3) the SDK version or curl command they used
support-bot: Helpful tip: our SDK injects X-Redwood-Request by default. if they used a proxy, it may strip that.
alex: if they don't have headers, ask them to reproduce with this curl and paste output:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  --verbose --compressed
```
maria: requesters often miss the 2xx vs 5xx body. ask them to copy the full HTTP response (status line + headers + body). short snippet doesn't help.
ryan: if they use our browser SDK, ask for Console > Network > click the failed request > copy as HAR. HAR is best since it preserves timing and headers.
emma: steps for SDK trace token: call `Redwood.getDebugToken()` (v2+ SDK) and send the token string. we can fetch server-side logs for that token.
alex: if they used mobile SDK, ask for device logs including any lines containing "X-Redwood-Request" or "rw-trace" — show example grep: `adb logcat | grep -i redwood`
maria: privacy note: ask them to redact Authorization and user PII before sharing. we only need the request id and payload shape. :lock:
ryan: minimal repro payload we want to reproduce: the exact JSON they sent (headers + body) and the timestamp window +- 2 minutes.
emma: if they can't reproduce live, ask for a HAR or a curl run with `-v` and `-D -` so headers show.
alex: internal triage: once we have the X-Redwood-Request value or rw-trace token, tag @ryan and include the timestamp window. we'll pull logs.
maria: quick troubleshooting commands we use: `rg "X-Redwood-Request|rw-trace" /var/log/redwood/*.log` on the pod logs.
support-bot: If customer sees no X-Redwood-Request: likely a proxy or CDN removed headers. ask for upstream load balancer config or CloudFront/NGINX rules.
emma: sample message customers can copy to their infra team: "Can you confirm if any proxy strips or rewrites request headers, specifically headers named 'X-Redwood-Request' or 'RW-Trace'."
ryan: when they give a debug token, we return a short debug-bundle id. ask them to upload any HAR + curl output to the ticket with that id.
alex: final quick checklist to send to customer in one paste: 1) Time of failed requests (UTC) 2) Full HTTP response (status+headers+body) 3) Full request (headers+body) or HAR 4) SDK version / curl command 5) Debug token from SDK if available 6) Indicate hosted/dedicated and region
maria: I'll draft a support reply and post to ticket. ping me in thread if you want me to escalate. :paperclip: 
ryan: thanks all — if we don't see X-Redwood-Request but do see other correlators (like request-id or traceparent) include them; we'll try correlating traces across proxies.
emma: tiny extra: if it's latency related, ask for timing fields from HAR (dns/connect/ttfb) and any client-side sampling rate.
alex: tagging this thread to ticket #INC-4951 when we have data. closing the loop once logs pulled. :white_check_mark:
